Defined in `src/diagrams_as_code/gantt.py`; import with `from diagrams_as_code.gantt import to_seconds`.

Seconds since the proleptic Gregorian origin; a date is its midnight.

## Kit module: `diagrams_as_code.text.math`

Source: `src/diagrams_as_code/text/math.py`.

A small TeX-like math typesetter that produces positioned glyph outlines.

Supported inside ``$...$``: letters (set in math italic), digits, sub/superscripts
with ``_`` and ``^``, ``{}`` grouping, Greek letters, the operators and relations
in ``SYMBOLS``, ``\mathrm{}`` / ``\text{}`` / ``\mathbf{}``, limits under big
operators, ``\frac{a}{b}`` fractions, ``\binom{n}{k}``, ``\sqrt{}`` and ``\sqrt[n]{}``,
``\bar{}``, ``\rightleftharpoons``, ``\ce{H2O}``, the accents ``\hat \tilde \dot \ddot \vec \grave`` and the spaces
``\,`` ``\;`` ``\quad``. This is not TeX: no matrices or ``\acute``/``\check``/``\breve``.

### `Glyph`

`class Glyph(cp: int, x: float, y: float, size: float) -> None`

Defined in `src/diagrams_as_code/text/math.py`; import with `from diagrams_as_code.text.math import Glyph`.

One outline to draw: codepoint, pen position (px, y down) and font size.

### `MathBox`

`class MathBox(width: float, height: float, depth: float, glyphs: tuple[Glyph, ...]) -> None`

Defined in `src/diagrams_as_code/text/math.py`; import with `from diagrams_as_code.text.math import MathBox`.

A typeset formula: its extent around the baseline and its glyphs.

Public members:

- `shifted(self, dx: float, dy: float) -> MathBox`: Return a copy with glyphs moved by (dx, dy) px; the baseline shift adjusts height and depth.

### `MathError`

`class MathError` extends `ValueError`

Defined in `src/diagrams_as_code/text/math.py`; import with `from diagrams_as_code.text.math import MathError`.

The formula uses something this typesetter does not support.

### `glyph_advance`

`def glyph_advance(cp: int, size: float) -> float`

Defined in `src/diagrams_as_code/text/math.py`; import with `from diagrams_as_code.text.math import glyph_advance`.

Horizontal advance in px of code point ``cp`` at font ``size`` px; raises KeyError if the glyph is missing.

### `glyph_available`

`def glyph_available(cp: int) -> bool`

Defined in `src/diagrams_as_code/text/math.py`; import with `from diagrams_as_code.text.math import glyph_available`.

True if the bundled math font has an outline for code point ``cp``.

### `glyph_path`

`def glyph_path(cp: int) -> str`

Defined in `src/diagrams_as_code/text/math.py`; import with `from diagrams_as_code.text.math import glyph_path`.

SVG path data of a glyph in font units, y axis pointing up.

### `typeset`

`def typeset(source: str, size: float) -> MathBox`

Defined in `src/diagrams_as_code/text/math.py`; import with `from diagrams_as_code.text.math import typeset`.

Typeset the formula ``source`` (without the ``$`` delimiters) at ``size`` px.

---

## Command-line interface

Exit codes: 0 success; 1 a script failed, lint found defects, or no diagram script was found; 2 usage error. Failures print `error: <path>: <message>` on stderr; `render` prints `wrote <path>` on stdout.

### `diagrams-as-code`

Render diagrams-as-code scripts.

#### `diagrams-as-code render`

render scripts or directories of scripts.

- `PATH`: one or more
- `--out OUT`: output directory (default: beside each script)
- `--format FORMAT`: comma-separated list from svg,png,pdf,bom (default: svg,bom)
- `--theme THEME`: one of blueprint, crimson, cyber_slate, dracula, emerald, high_contrast, iiot_dark_gold, iiot_light, monochrome, nord, paper, pastel_light, solarized_light, synthwave
- `--interactive`: emit interactive pan/zoom-enabled SVG output
- `--no-interactive`: disable interactive SVG output
- `--layout LAYOUT`: one of manual, auto
- `--direction DIRECTION`: one of LR, TB
- `--layout-file LAYOUT_FILE`
- `--debug`: show tracebacks
- `--json`: print one JSON document on stdout and nothing else (diagnostics on stderr)

#### `diagrams-as-code lint`

Lay out each diagram and report what a reader would see as a defect: a line through a node, labels on top of each other, text spilling out of its box. Exits 1 if anything is found.

- `PATH`: one or more
- `--ignore KIND[,KIND]`: defect kinds not to report; choose from edge_through_node, edge_through_own_endpoint, tangent_arrival, edge_on_edge, edge_through_badge, badge_over_node, badge_over_badge, badge_over_title, edge_through_title, title_overflow, label_overflow, node_overlap, group_overlap, content_clipped, canvas_mostly_empty
- `--quiet`: print findings only, no summary
- `--layout LAYOUT`: one of manual, auto
- `--direction DIRECTION`: one of LR, TB
- `--layout-file LAYOUT_FILE`
- `--debug`: show tracebacks
- `--json`: print one JSON document on stdout and nothing else (diagnostics on stderr)

#### `diagrams-as-code layout`

layout file tools.

##### `diagrams-as-code layout export`

write a script's positions to a layout file.

- `script`
- `-o, --output OUTPUT`
- `--layout LAYOUT`: one of manual, auto
- `--direction DIRECTION`: one of LR, TB
- `--layout-file LAYOUT_FILE`
- `--debug`: show tracebacks

#### `diagrams-as-code mcp`

serve render/lint/list tools over MCP (stdio).

- `--root ROOT`: directory scripts and outputs are confined to (default: .)
- `--timeout SECONDS`: wall-clock limit for one script (default: 60)
- `--memory-mb MB`: memory limit for one script, POSIX (default: 2048)

#### `diagrams-as-code themes`

list built-in themes.

- `--json`: print one JSON document on stdout and nothing else (diagnostics on stderr)

#### `diagrams-as-code icons`

list built-in icons.

- `--domain DOMAIN`
- `--json`: print one JSON document on stdout and nothing else (diagnostics on stderr)

#### `diagrams-as-code api`

List every name in diagrams_as_code.__all__ and the plot, draft, sequence and gantt kits with kind, signature and a one-line summary. NAME narrows it (a class, function, kit module or substring); a class also lists its methods. Exits 1 if NAME matches nothing.

- `NAME`
- `--json`: print one JSON document on stdout and nothing else (diagnostics on stderr)

#### `diagrams-as-code examples`

List example scripts as DOMAIN/NAME with a title. Without --domain, list domains with their counts instead.

- `--domain DOMAIN`: only this domain (e.g. finance, cad)
- `--dir DIR`: examples directory (default: ./examples, else the checkout's)
- `--json`: print one JSON document on stdout and nothing else (diagnostics on stderr)

#### `diagrams-as-code source`

Print the script of an example, DOMAIN/NAME (the numeric prefix of NAME is optional) or a NAME unique in the gallery. Exits 1 if there is no such example.

- `EXAMPLE`
- `--dir DIR`: examples directory (default: ./examples, else the checkout's)

---

## MCP server tools

Start with `diagrams-as-code mcp --root DIR`. JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio. Script and output paths are confined to `DIR`; each script runs in a resource-limited child process (no file or network isolation).

### `list_examples`

List diagram scripts under a directory, with the SVG rendered beside each.

Input schema:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "path": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "directory, default 'examples'"
    },
    "domain": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "e.g. finance, physics, cad"
    }
  },
  "required": [],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

### `render`

Render a diagram script file (or every script in a directory) under the server root. Output goes beside the script unless 'out' is given. To render script text you have no file for, use render_source.

Input schema:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "path": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "script or directory, relative to the root"
    },
    "out": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "output directory under the root"
    },
    "formats": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "enum": [
          "svg",
          "png",
          "pdf",
          "bom"
        ]
      },
      "uniqueItems": true,
      "description": "svg, png, pdf (binary: need out) and bom (a Markdown bill of materials)"
    },
    "theme": {
      "enum": [
        "blueprint",
        "crimson",
        "cyber_slate",
        "dracula",
        "emerald",
        "high_contrast",
        "iiot_dark_gold",
        "iiot_light",
        "monochrome",
        "nord",
        "paper",
        "pastel_light",
        "solarized_light",
        "synthwave"
      ],
      "description": "overrides the script's own theme"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "path"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

### `lint`

Report visual defects (overlaps, clipped text, lines through nodes) in diagram script files. For script text, use lint_source.

Input schema:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "path": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "script or directory, relative to the root"
    },
    "ignore": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "enum": [
          "edge_through_node",
          "edge_through_own_endpoint",
          "tangent_arrival",
          "edge_on_edge",
          "edge_through_badge",
          "badge_over_node",
          "badge_over_badge",
          "badge_over_title",
          "edge_through_title",
          "title_overflow",
          "label_overflow",
          "node_overlap",
          "group_overlap",
          "content_clipped",
          "canvas_mostly_empty"
        ]
      },
      "description": "defect kinds not to report"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "path"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

### `render_source`

Render diagram script TEXT (a program defining diagram() -> Diagram) without any file. Returns the SVG inline (default when 'out' is omitted; cut at 100000 characters, see svg_truncated) and/or writes files under 'out' inside the server root. The source runs as arbitrary Python in the sandbox (timeout, CPU/memory caps, no stdin/stdout); it is not file or network isolation. Output is byte-identical to render of the same script.

Input schema:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "source": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Python text defining diagram() -> Diagram (see describe_api, get_example); at most 200000 characters. It RUNS as arbitrary Python in the resource-limited sandbox"
    },
    "formats": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "enum": [
          "svg",
          "png",
          "pdf",
          "bom"
        ]
      },
      "uniqueItems": true,
      "description": "svg, png, pdf (binary: need out) and bom (a Markdown bill of materials)"
    },
    "theme": {
      "enum": [
        "blueprint",
        "crimson",
        "cyber_slate",
        "dracula",
        "emerald",
        "high_contrast",
        "iiot_dark_gold",
        "iiot_light",
        "monochrome",
        "nord",
        "paper",
        "pastel_light",
        "solarized_light",
        "synthwave"
      ],
      "description": "overrides the script's own theme"
    },
    "inline": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "return the SVG (and bom) text; default true when 'out' is omitted, false otherwise"
    },
    "out": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "directory under the root to write files into"
    },
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "output file stem; default the script's OUTPUT_STEM or 'script'"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "source"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

### `lint_source`

Input schema:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "source": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Python text defining diagram() -> Diagram (see describe_api, get_example); at most 200000 characters. It RUNS as arbitrary Python in the resource-limited sandbox"
    },
    "ignore": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "enum": [
          "edge_through_node",
          "edge_through_own_endpoint",
          "tangent_arrival",
          "edge_on_edge",
          "edge_through_badge",
          "badge_over_node",
          "badge_over_badge",
          "badge_over_title",
          "edge_through_title",
          "title_overflow",
          "label_overflow",
          "node_overlap",
          "group_overlap",
          "content_clipped",
          "canvas_mostly_empty"
        ]
      },
      "description": "defect kinds not to report"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "source"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

### `get_example`

Return one gallery example's script text and its committed SVG: a working template to adapt for render_source. Find names with list_domains.

Input schema:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "domain": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "gallery domain, e.g. finance, cad, iiot ('root' for the top-level scripts)"
    },
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "script stem, e.g. 01_candlestick_chart; the numeric prefix may be omitted"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "domain",
    "name"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

### `list_domains`

List the example gallery's domains with the number and titles of the examples in each.

Input schema:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {},
  "required": [],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

### `describe_api`

Structured reference of the public Python API a diagram script can use: every name in diagrams_as_code.__all__ plus the kit modules plot, draft, sequence and gantt, each with kind, signature and a one-line summary, built by introspection. Pass 'name' (a class or function, a kit module such as 'gantt', or a substring) to narrow it; one or a few matching classes also list their methods.

Input schema:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "exact name, kit module or substring, case-insensitive"
    }
  },
  "required": [],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

### `capabilities`

Summary of docs/capabilities.json, the project's verified capability manifest: ids, titles, categories, status and the command that verifies each.

Input schema:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "category": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "only this category"
    }
  },
  "required": [],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

### `list_themes`

List built-in themes.

Input schema:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {},
  "required": [],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

### `list_icons`

List built-in icons, optionally for one domain.

Input schema:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "domain": {
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

# Math markup reference

Text between `$` signs in any label, title, note or caption is typeset as mathematics. The syntax is a subset of TeX. Math is drawn as vector outlines from a bundled open-licensed font (STIX Two Math), so it looks the same in every browser, in PNG and in print.

```python
d.shape(r"**Policy**\n$\Pi(E_t, E_{t+1}) \to \{\mathrm{allow}, \mathrm{deny}\}$", 260, 70)
d.text(r"$\Omega_{\mathrm{safe}} = \bigcap_{k} \Omega_k$", size=16)
```

Use a raw string (`r"..."`) or double the backslashes. A literal dollar sign is `\$`; a lone `$` with no partner (`"Under $50k"`) is left as text.

Anything outside this reference raises `MathError` naming the command, instead of drawing something wrong. To check a formula before using it:

```python
from diagrams_as_code.text import TextStyle, layout

layout(r"$\theta \leftarrow \theta - \eta \nabla_\theta L$", TextStyle(size=13))
```

## Basics

| Write | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `x`, `E`, `f` | letters are set in math italic |
| `0`–`9` | digits are upright |
| `x_i`, `x_{t+1}` | subscript: one character, or a `{group}` |
| `x^2`, `e^{-st}` | superscript |
| `x_i^2` | both |
| `{...}` | a group, treated as one item |
| `\{`, `\}` | literal braces |
| `+ - * / = < > ( ) [ ] \| , ; : ! ' .` | typed as they are, spaced by their role |

Spacing follows the role of each symbol: binary operators and relations get space around them, punctuation gets space after it, and scripts are set tight.

## Text and fonts in math

| Write | Result |
|---|---|
| `\mathrm{safe}`, `\text{safe}`, `\textrm{safe}` | upright text |
| `\mathbf{R}`, `\textbf{R}` | bold upright |
| `\mathit{max}` | italic as a word, not as a product of letters |
| `\operatorname{rank}` | upright, spaced as an operator |
| `\mathbb{R}` | blackboard bold; `R N Z Q C` only |

## Greek

Lowercase: `\alpha \beta \gamma \delta \epsilon \zeta \eta \theta \iota \kappa \lambda \mu \nu \xi \omicron \pi \rho \varsigma \sigma \tau \upsilon \phi \chi \psi \omega`, and the variants `\varepsilon \vartheta \varphi \varrho \varpi`.

Uppercase: `\Gamma \Delta \Theta \Lambda \Xi \Pi \Sigma \Upsilon \Phi \Psi \Omega`. The other capitals are the Latin letters.

## Symbols

| Kind | Commands |
|---|---|
| Ordinary | `\partial \nabla \infty \forall \exists \nexists \emptyset \ell \hbar \top \bot \neg \lnot \angle \prime \ldots \dots \cdots \vdots \vert \Vert` |
| Binary operators | `\pm \mp \times \div \cdot \ast \circ \bullet \land \wedge \lor \vee \cap \cup \setminus \oplus \ominus \otimes \odot \sqcap \sqcup \uplus \diamond` |
| Relations | `\leq \le \geq \ge \neq \ne \equiv \approx \sim \simeq \cong \propto \ll \gg \prec \succ \preceq \succeq \triangleq \coloneqq` |
| Sets | `\in \notin \ni \subset \supset \subseteq \supseteq \subsetneq \supsetneq \sqsubseteq \sqsupseteq` |
| Logic and geometry | `\mid \parallel \perp \vdash \dashv \models` |
| Arrows | `\to \rightarrow \leftarrow \gets \leftrightarrow \uparrow \downarrow \mapsto \Rightarrow \Leftarrow \Leftrightarrow \implies \iff \longrightarrow \longleftarrow \leadsto \rightsquigarrow \rightleftharpoons \rightleftarrows` |
| Delimiters | `\langle \rangle \lceil \rceil \lfloor \rfloor \lbrace \rbrace` |
| Punctuation | `\colon` |

`\rightleftharpoons` and `\rightleftarrows` both draw an equilibrium sign as a right arrow stacked over a left arrow. The outline set has no half-arrow (harpoon) glyph, so this is the double-arrow style, not the harpoon one.

## Chemical formulas

`\ce{...}` sets a formula upright and fills in the subscripts: `\ce{H2O}`, `\ce{Ca(OH)2}`. Digits after a letter, `)` or `]` become subscripts; a `+` or `-` stuck to a species and ending it is a charge (`\ce{NH4+}`); `^` takes a charge or exponent run (`\ce{SO4^2-}`, `\ce{Fe^3+}`); `->` and `<=>` become `\rightarrow` and `\rightleftharpoons`. A spaced `+` stays a plus (`\ce{2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O}`). Leading digits are coefficients. This is a typesetting helper, not a chemistry parser: no isotopes, bond symbols or state-specific rules. Writing `\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}` explicitly still works.

## Functions and big operators

Named functions are set upright: `\min \max \sup \inf \lim \limsup \liminf \arg \argmin \argmax \log \ln \lg \exp \sin \cos \tan \cot \sec \csc \sinh \cosh \tanh \coth \arcsin \arccos \arctan \det \dim \ker \hom \Pr \gcd \deg`.

As in TeX, `\min \max \sup \inf \lim \limsup \liminf \argmin \argmax \det \gcd \Pr` put a subscript underneath (`\lim_{x \to 0}`); the others set scripts beside the name (`\cos^2 \theta`, `\sin^{-1} x`).

## Bars and roots

`\bar x`, `\bar{x}` and `\overline{AB}` draw a bar over their argument. `\sqrt{x}` draws a radical with a bar over its argument: `\sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}`. The bar is the minus-sign outline repeated, so it is a little thinner than a typeset rule and the radical does not stretch past one line of text. `\sqrt[n]{x}` tucks a reduced-size index into the crook of the radical: `\sqrt[3]{x}`, `\sqrt[n]{x^2+1}`.

`\frac{a}{b}` (also `\dfrac`, `\tfrac`) stacks the numerator over the denominator about a rule on the math axis, both centred and set at 85% of the surrounding size; a fraction inside a fraction shrinks again. Like the bar, the rule is the minus-sign outline repeated. `\over` is not supported.

`\binom{n}{k}` stacks two entries with no rule between parentheses that grow to the height of the stack: `\binom{n}{k} = \frac{n!}{k!(n-k)!}`.

## Accents

`\hat{x}`, `\tilde{y}`, `\dot{a}`, `\ddot{a}`, `\vec{v}` and `\grave{e}` centre a mark over their argument, just clear of its top; `\widehat` and `\widetilde` use a larger mark for wide arguments. The mark is a single glyph, so it does not stretch to the argument's width. `\acute`, `\check` and `\breve` are not available: the outline set has no such mark.

Big operators: `\sum \prod \coprod \int \oint \bigcap \bigcup \bigwedge \bigvee`. Their limits are set underneath and above:

```text
$\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i$        $\bigcap_{k} \Omega_k$
```

Add `\nolimits` to set them beside the operator, or `\limits` to force them underneath:

```text
$\sum\nolimits_{i} x_i$
```

## Spaces

| Write | Width |
|---|---|
| `\,` | thin |
| `\:` | medium |
| `\;` | thick |
| `\!` | negative thin |
| `\ ` (backslash, space) | a word space |
| `\quad`, `\qquad` | one em, two ems |

`\left`, `\right`, `\displaystyle` and `\textstyle` are accepted and ignored, so formulas pasted from a paper need less editing. Delimiters do not grow.

## Not supported

These raise `MathError`:

| Not supported | Write instead |
|---|---|
| matrices, `\begin{...}` | one `d.text()` per row, or a table of shapes |
| `\acute \check \breve` accents | `\hat`, `\tilde`, or a prime: `y'` |
| `\mathcal`, `\mathfrak` | `\mathbf` or a Greek letter |
| stretchy delimiters | plain `( )`, `[ ]`, `\langle \rangle` |

## Mixing math and text

Math and markup combine freely in one label, and lines break only outside math:

```python
d.text(
    "Valid$(a_i, I)$ = Provenance$(a_i, I) \\land$ Capability$(a_i, I)$\n"
    "*holds for every action* $a_i$",
    size=14, align="center",
)
```

Label width is measured from the same outlines that are drawn, so a shape grows to fit a formula just as it does for plain text.
